newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cambodian prince expects new setback to homecoming.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian prince expects new setback to homecoming.

text.p: Cambodia's exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh, accused of plotting to kill Cambodian Co-Premier Hun Sen, said on Wednesday he expected his country's national airline would bar him from flying home.

Sirivudh told Reuters he was still trying to book a Thursday flight on Royal Air Cambodge but he was not hopeful after an abortive attempt on Tuesday when Hong Kong's Dragonair refused to fly him to Phnom Penh, fearing trouble on arrival there.

Phnom Penh has threatened to arrest Sirivudh if he returns, and reports from the capital have said the government might send troops to meet his flight. But the prince told Reuters he would still try to get a seat with Air Cambodge.
"I've asked my colleaques to check on this now. Still wait for the answer," he said by telephone from a hotel room in Hong Kong, where he arrived on Tuesday from Germany.
"I had indication from Mr Audre Lim, the Consul here...that Air Cambodge will be (putting) me in trouble again. It seems that we cannot even book a reservation," he said.

Sirivudh said on Tuesday he would persist in attempts to go home for a fair trial. A half brother of King Norodom Sihanouk and a former foreign minister, Sirivudh went into exile in December 1995 after being held for one month on charges of involvement in an alleged plot against the life of Hun Sen.
